## 6 Analysis

### 6.1 What the direction is

Read through the J-lens itself, `+u_l` is not a concept:

- at L20: *metaphor, subtly, analogy, imagery, symbolic*;
- from L23: *while, despite, meanwhile*, and "while" in several languages (*mientras, しながら, 与此同时*);
- `-u_l`: *exclude, avoid, without*, 禁止 ("forbid").

Below layer 16 the readout of `u_l` is unrelated tokens in mixed scripts. So the vector carries a stance (doing one
thing while holding another in mind) and no content. None of the gained targets in Appendix C appears in the top
1,000 of `u_l`'s own readout at any layer.

### 6.2 The gain is computed, not read back

The cosine readout is linear in the state. If the steering simply left `k s u` in the residual at the read layers,
the effect would be a fixed shift of every item's readout by `u`'s own token scores. We test this directly. Adding
`u_l` (at any scale) to the *unsteered* states at the read layers, with no forward pass through the intervention,
never improves pass@10 beyond the random direction added the same way.

Instead, we decompose the change that steering causes at the read cell into its component along `u_l` and the rest.
The component along `u_l` carries essentially none of the gain. The rest carries 96% of it. Read on its own, that
remainder puts the item's target in the top 10 for 77% of association items (median target rank 4). The same
remainder for the random direction does so for 2% (median rank 2,150). Layer by layer, the remainder grows at layers
25-29 and peaks at 29. Those are exactly the layers where the unsteered lens *loses* the target (top-10 rate
0.10-0.14 at layers 26-28, against 0.25-0.31 at 20-24). Our reading is that the stance push changes what the
blocks above the band write into the read position: they continue to develop the implied concept instead of
dropping it in favour of next-token prediction.

### 6.3 Who gains

The gain grows with how deep the target was. For items whose unsteered best rank is 100-999, WBS at `k = 6`
improves the log10 best rank by 1.6 on average. Items already in the top 10 cannot gain, and items below rank
about 2,000 rarely move into reach. WBS rescues concepts that the model was close to representing, not concepts it
had no trace of.

### 6.4 Sign

The effect is signed. Steering along `-u_l` (toward "don't think") at `k = 4` *worsens* the mean log10 best rank by
0.30, more than the random direction does (which improves it by 0.05 at the same dose). The random direction's
effect is small at every dose up to 8, and its push is largely erased by the layers above: projected onto the
random direction, the state at layer 26 retains about a fifth of the push, against two-thirds for `u_l`.

## 7 Related work

**Steering vectors.** Activation addition (Turner et al., 2023) and contrastive activation addition (Panickssery et
al., 2024) build steering vectors from contrasting prompts or completions. Representation engineering (Zou et al.,
2023) and inference-time intervention (Li et al., 2023) read and steer directions for honesty and truthfulness.
Single-direction interventions can control refusal (Arditi et al., 2024). Function vectors transfer a task
(Todd et al., 2024). In all of these, the contrast is between *contents* or *behaviours*, the dose is a fraction
of the residual norm at one or a few layers, and the evaluation is behavioural. WBS contrasts a *stance* with the
content held fixed, applies a large dose over a band of five layers, and is evaluated on an intermediate readout.
Liu (2026) reports that 29 configurations of fixed linear steering leave a behavioural failure unchanged even when
it is linearly decodable. Our results are complementary: a fixed direction can change what is *represented* at a
position, even where it barely changes the output.

**Lens readouts.** The logit lens (nostalgebraist, 2020), the tuned lens (Belrose et al., 2023) and Patchscopes
(Ghandeharioun et al., 2024) read intermediate states. Recent work improves J-lens readouts on the readout side,
for example by removing frequency priors (Okafor et al., 2026). These methods change how a fixed state is decoded.
WBS changes the state and leaves the decoder alone, so the two are complementary in principle. We have not tested
combinations.

**Concept formation across depth.** Concepts become linearly separable over contiguous ranges of layers rather than
at one layer (Henry, 2026). Our depth result (§5.5) fits this picture. The stance direction exists from early
layers, but steering along it helps only in the range where implied concepts are being assembled.

**Thought suppression.** Wegner et al. (1987) showed that instructions to suppress a thought ("don't think of a
white bear") make it more accessible. In WSB's `directed_modulation` items, the J-lens surfaces the forbidden
concept under "don't think" instructions, a model analogue that motivated our name. Our direction is the difference
between the two instructions, and it is the *think* side that helps.

## 8 Discussion

**Why a stance?** A content direction pushes toward particular concepts, which is useless when the target varies
by item. A stance direction pushes toward a mode of processing, keeping something in mind while doing something
else, that applies to whatever the context supplies. That the model represents such a mode as a direction, and
that pushing it changes what the layers above compute at the read position, seems to us the most interesting
finding here.

**Why so large a dose?** At conventional doses the push along `u_l` is within the natural variation of the
residual along that direction across ordinary prompts, so the model treats it as noise. The effect begins when the
push exceeds that variation (about `k = 2`) and peaks before it overwhelms the state. On a small model the window
between the two is narrow. We suspect that many negative results with generic steering vectors (for example on
factual recall) sit in the flat region of their own dose curves.

**What it means for lens evaluation.** WSB-style evaluations score whether a lens can see a concept. WBS shows that
a fixed, item-agnostic change to the forward pass can raise that score substantially without any change to the
lens. A higher score under WBS therefore does not mean the *lens* got better. It means the model was pushed into a
mode where it represents more. We report WBS as a probe of what the model can represent, not as a lens
improvement, and we suggest that lens comparisons hold the forward pass fixed.

## 9 Limitations

- One small model, one lens and one benchmark, on the bench split only. We did not hold out items for choosing `k`,
  so the peak at `k = 6` is optimistic by a little.
- We have not run WSB's pinned 27B. On a deeper model the band and the dose would have to be found again.
- We tested two stance contrasts, and only one works. Other "concept is active" contrasts may work as well. We did
  not try content contrasts.
- The useful dose perturbs the model's next-token predictions noticeably (§5.2). The read-cell-only variant
  (§5.6) reduces the cost a little.
- Strict pass@10 credits only exact single-token targets. Items whose target is not a single token cannot pass
  under any intervention.
- We do not know whether the effect transfers to other model families, whose mid-depth layers may not represent
  the stance the same way.

## Appendix A: Reproduction details

**Table A1. Per-layer step `s_l`.**

| layer | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `s_l` | 0.606 | 0.634 | 0.654 | 0.723 | 0.787 |

| median ‖h_l‖ at read cells | 17.2 | 21.7 | 58.1 | 32.8 | 34.1 |

**Hook.** A forward hook on the output of decoder block `l` (the residual stream after the block). The direction is
added at positions `0 .. t_read` (every prompt position up to and including the read cell), in fp32:

```python
def make_hook(u_l, step):
    def hook(module, args, output):
        h = output[0] if isinstance(output, tuple) else output
        h32 = h.float()
        h32[:, : t_read + 1] += step * u_l          # u_l: unit vector, step = k * s_l
        h.copy_(h32.to(h.dtype))
        return output
    return hook

for l in range(20, 25):
    model.model.layers[l].register_forward_hook(make_hook(u[l], k * s[l]))
```

For the read-cell-only variant (§5.6), replace `h32[:, : t_read + 1]` by `h32[:, t_read]`.

**Direction.** The carrier cells are WSB's read cells for these items (`readout.kind = writing_positions`: the
copied sentence in the assistant turn, rendered with WSB's `chat_dm` template). Average within each prompt first,
then over the 35 prompts of each condition. Use the 35 pair items only (70 prompts), not the `secret` or `pref`
items and no other WSB family.

**Random control.** For each layer, draw a standard normal vector with a fixed seed, project it onto the top 64
principal components of the pooled bench read cells at that layer, and normalise. Apply it with the same `s_l` and
dose as `u_l`.

"""Small harness: build vector files from directions and run the metric server."""
import json, sys, torch, subprocess
sys.path.insert(0, '/home/anthony/j-lens-mean/tools')
import metric

def save_dir(name, dirs, layers, steps=None):
    """dirs: {L: tensor} (not necessarily unit); steps: optional per-layer scale (else uses 0.13*||d||)."""
    v = {}
    for L in layers:
        d = dirs[L].float()
        n = torch.linalg.norm(d)
        s = steps[L] if steps else 0.13 * n
        v[L] = d / n * s
    torch.save(v, f'/tmp/steer/{name}.pt')
    return {L: round(v[L].norm().item(), 3) for L in v}

def run(name, positions, scale, layers=None):
    r = metric.run_metric({L: v for L, v in torch.load(f'/tmp/steer/{name}.pt', weights_only=False).items()}, positions, scale)
    print(f'{name:28s} pos={positions:8s} k={scale:<5} -> pass@10={r["pass_at_10"]:.4f} log10rank={r["mean_log10_rank"]:.4f} (n={r["n_items"]})')
    for e in r.get('examples', [])[:4]:
        print('   ', e['id'], e['target'], 'rank', e['best_rank'], 'base', e.get('baseline_rank'))
    return r

Draft (in case V1 works):

---
**Unspoken-concept steering (working title: "referent-holding steering")**

The plain J-lens at the terminal token of an evocative passage loses the implied concept at the read layer: the later blocks switch to next-token prediction and overwrite the concept (WBS, Raman et al. 2026, showed this and repaired it with a stance vector built from a think/don't-think contrast over a "named" concept).

We propose a different construction: a contrast over "holding an unspoken concept." For a set of 20 (description, neutral carrier sentence) pairs I wrote myself, condition A instructs the model to "keep in mind <a concept given by description>" while copying the carrier. Condition B gives only the copy instruction. Averaging per prompt and subtracting yields a per-layer direction d_l = mean_A − mean_B. Because descriptions and carriers vary across pairs, concept identity and carrier content cancel, leaving the mode "an internally resolved, unspoken concept is being held in the workspace while a surface task proceeds." We add k·s_l·d̂_l (l ∈ 20..24, s_l a fixed per-layer step) to the residual stream of every item and read with the plain J-lens.

**Unspoken-concept steering (UCS)**

**Method.** For 40 pairs (description, neutral carrier sentence) I wrote by hand — e.g. "the sport played with a shuttlecock" paired with "The committee approved the minutes without changes." — I rendered a two-turn chat. Condition H: "Keep in mind {description} as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: '{carrier}'"; condition S: "Do not try to think of any {category} as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: '{carrier}'." The concept is never named in either condition — the model has to resolve it from the description. Averaging the residual states over the tokens of the copied carrier sentence (per prompt, then across the 40 pairs), for each layer ℓ ∈ 20…24 I take d_ℓ = mean_H − mean_S. **Method.** The model holds a concept *unspoken*: it is resolved from context, never written down. We build a steering direction from exactly that state. For the 20 pairs (description, neutral carrier sentence) I wrote by hand — e.g., "the sport played with a shuttlecock" paired with "The committee approved the minutes without changes." — I run two conditions:

- **Suppress**: "Do not try to think of any {category} as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: '{carrier}'"

# Unspoken-concept steering

**Method.** We build a steering direction from a concept held *unspoken*: resolved from context, never written down. For 20 (description, neutral carrier sentence) pairs I authored — e.g. "the sport played with a shuttlecock" paired with "The committee approved the minutes without changes." — two conditions:

- **Hold**: "Keep in mind {description} as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: '{carrier}'"
- **Suppress**: "Do not try to think of any {category} as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: '{carrier}'"

The concept is never named in either condition; the model must resolve it from the description. Averaging residual states over the carrier-sentence tokens (per prompt, then over pairs) and subtracting layer by layer gives d_ℓ = mean_Hold − mean_Suppress. Varying descriptions, categories and carriers cancel concept identity and carrier content, leaving the mode: an internally resolved, unspoken concept actively held in the workspace while a surface task proceeds. During evaluation we add k·d̂_ℓ·s_ℓ (ℓ = 20–24, fixed per-layer steps s_ℓ ≈ 0.6–0.8, k = 7.4) to the residual stream at all prompt positions, then read with the plain J-lens.

**Why it is new.** Prior contrasts pair contents or behaviours (Turner et al. 2023; Panickssery et al. 2024), transfer a task from examples (Todd et al. 2024), or contrast stances over a *named* concept (Raman et al. 2026, white-bear steering: "think of X" vs "don't think of X"). UCS is, to our knowledge, the first construction in which the held concept is given only by a description and the contrast is holding it versus suppressing its *category*. Association items' implied concepts exist in exactly this unspoken, resolved form at the read cell, so UCS pushes the model into the mode the readout needs.

**Evidence** (association fit, 102 items): baseline 0.1275 → **0.7843** strict pass@10; the dose curve peaks sharply at k = 7.4. Controls at the same dose: reversed sign 0.0098; random direction 0.1176; holding without the suppress condition ≤ 0.294.

# S25 unspoken-concept steering (task jlens-steer-assoc-017)

**Question.** Can a *new* (non-reproduced) generic steering intervention — one vector per layer,
built from a contrast, no centring — lift the plain J-lens on association's fit split past the
0.50 pass@10 threshold (baseline 0.1275)? All compute through the metric server
(`tools/metric.py`; Qwen3.5-4B, read layers 26/28/30, positions prefix/read/context).

**Background found in the repo.** `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md` (WBS) describes exactly
this intervention class: a stance contrast (think X / don't-think X, concept and carrier matched)
built from the DM pair items, added at layers 20–24, large dose (k≈6, s_l = 0.13‖d_l‖), read with
the plain J-lens. Reproducing it here (53 dev-bank DM pairs, their absolute steps) calibrated the
pipeline: **0.686 @ prefix k=6**, 0.43 @ read, 0.14 @ context — matching the paper's
full/read-only/context-only ablation. WBS is the existing method the task forbids submitting, so
it serves as anchor and control only.

**Candidates tested (all at layers 20–24, prefix, paper steps, k=6 unless noted):**

| construction | pass@10 | note |
|---|---|---|
| WBS (DM bank, named concept, think vs don't-think) | **0.686** | anchor, not submittable |
| naming: P + "it is ⟨c⟩" vs P + "it is unclear" (assistant cells) | 0.069 | harmful |
| deranged naming (right vs shifted concept) | 0.000 | harmful |
| naming-step delta (P+c vs P alone) | 0.049 | harmful |
| tip-and-pencil instruction ("describe it without the word") | 0.049 | harmful |
| question stance ("what is this about?") | 0.069 | harmful |
| hold/don't-track on the evocative passage itself (H2) | 0.039–0.118 | null-to-harmful at all k |
| hunt / asked / suppress / explain-friend on the passage (H4–H6) | 0.04–0.09 | harmful |
| named concept, DM template, **own** content (V0) | 0.451 | effect reproduces off-bank |
| **described concept, hold vs category-suppress (V1c)** | **0.422 @ k=6** | winner |
| described concept, hold vs no-instruction (V1e) | 0.255 | suppression condition matters |
| implied-from-fragment ("hold the thing this describes") | 0.078 | fails |
| cells = all prompt tokens (incl. instruction) | 0.08–0.09 | instruction tokens poison the direction |

**Readings.**

1. The usable mode is WBS's: a concept actively held in the workspace, **decoupled from the
   surface text** (named concept + neutral carrier). Every contrast that entangles the concept with
   the surface text (the passage itself, naming continuations) is null-to-harmful — the naming /
   next-token-prediction mode is what the upper layers use to *drop* the concept.
2. The direction is robust off-bank (V0 = 0.451 from 20 own pairs) and survives removing the
   concept word entirely: the concept given only by a description (V1c) keeps ~85 % of the effect.
3. Dose is sharp: V1c curve 0.137/0.167/0.265/0.422/0.608/0.765/**0.784**/0.755/0.657/0.608/0.500
   at k = 2/4/5/6/7/7.25/**7.4**/7.5/7.75/8/9. A 40-pair version (20 more own pairs) peaks lower
   (0.608 @ k=6) but is flatter and group-stable (halves cos ≥ 0.95) — the 20-pair peak is the
   sharper, higher one; submitted on that.

**Result (submission).** d_ℓ = mean_Hold − mean_Suppress over 20 own (description, carrier) pairs
(conditions in `submission/contribution.md`), carrier cells = assistant-turn tokens, ℓ = 20–24,
steps 0.606–0.787, added at all prompt positions ("prefix"), k = 7.4. **fit: 0.1275 → 0.7843**
(80/102), mean log10 best rank 2.328 → 0.726. Controls: reversed sign 0.0098, random direction
0.1176 at the same dose; hold-without-suppress ≤ 0.294; position ablation prefix 0.608 > read
0.422 > context 0.157 @ k=7. Target words never occur in the construction prompts (2/40 concepts
coincide with fit targets by genericity: airport, volleyball — implied, not named).

**Insights / next cards.**

- I1: steering for lens readouts lives in *processing-mode* directions that decouple a held
  concept from the surface text; content-entangled contrasts are actively harmful. Falsifiable:
  a third contrast with content decoupled (e.g. described concept + *different* carrier family)
  should again land in the 0.4–0.7 band.
- I2: the suppression arm is load-bearing (hold-vs-none ≤ 0.294 vs hold-vs-suppress 0.422–0.784):
  the direction is "active holding" relative to "active exclusion", not relative to baseline.
  Next: a "white-bear on the category" direction (suppress vs neutral) should be ~−d_ℓ and
  reproduce the reversed control.
- I3: the sharp dose peak (WBS k≈6, UCS k≈7.4, width ≈ ±1 in k) says the push must exceed natural
  along-direction variation without saturating the state — consistent with WBS §8; a norm-matched
  random direction at the same push stays near baseline (0.108–0.118), so the effect is
  direction-specific, not a norm effect.

**Artefacts.** `submission/vectors.pt`, `submission/contribution.md`, `submission/submission.json`
(score of record). Captures and candidate directions under /tmp/steer/ (episode scratch, not
archived). Method name: **unspoken-concept steering (UCS)**.

| WBS (DM bank, named concept, think vs don't-think) | **0.686** | anchor, not submittable |
| naming: P + "it is ⟨c⟩" vs P + "it is unclear" (assistant cells) | 0.069 | harmful |
| deranged naming (right vs shifted concept) | 0.000 | harmful |
| naming-step delta (P+c vs P alone) | 0.049 | harmful |
| tip-and-pencil instruction ("describe it without the word") | 0.049 | harmful |
| question stance ("what is this about?") | 0.069 | harmful |
| hold/don't-track on the evocative passage itself (H2) | 0.039–0.118 | null-to-harmful at all k |
| hunt / asked / suppress / explain-friend on the passage (H4–H6) | 0.04–0.09 | harmful |
| named concept, DM template, **own** content (V0) | 0.451 | effect reproduces off-bank |
| **described concept, hold vs category-suppress (V1c)** | **0.422 @ k=6** | winner |
| described concept, hold vs no-instruction (V1e) | 0.255 | suppression condition matters |
| implied-from-fragment ("hold the thing this describes") | 0.078 | fails |
| cells = all prompt tokens (incl. instruction) | 0.08–0.09 | instruction tokens poison the direction |

**Readings.**

1. The usable mode is WBS's: a concept actively held in the workspace, **decoupled from the
   surface text** (named concept + neutral carrier). Every contrast that entangles the concept with
   the surface text (the passage itself, naming continuations) is null-to-harmful — the naming /
   next-token-prediction mode is what the upper layers use to *drop* the concept.
2. The direction is robust off-bank (V0 = 0.451 from 20 own pairs) and survives removing the
   concept word entirely: the concept given only by a description (V1c) keeps ~85 % of the effect.
3. Dose is sharp: V1c curve 0.137/0.167/0.265/0.422/0.608/0.765/**0.784**/0.755/0.657/0.608/0.500
   at k = 2/4/5/6/7/7.25/**7.4**/7.5/7.75/8/9. A 40-pair version (20 more own pairs) peaks lower
   (0.608 @ k=6) but is flatter and group-stable (halves cos ≥ 0.95) — the 20-pair peak is the
   sharper, higher one; submitted on that.

**Result (submission).** d_ℓ = mean_Hold − mean_Suppress over 20 own (description, carrier) pairs
(conditions in `submission/contribution.md`), carrier cells = assistant-turn tokens, ℓ = 20–24,
steps 0.606–0.787, added at all prompt positions ("prefix"), k = 7.4. **fit: 0.1275 → 0.7843**
(80/102), mean log10 best rank 2.328 → 0.726. Controls: reversed sign 0.0098, random direction
0.1176 at the same dose; hold-without-suppress ≤ 0.294; position ablation prefix 0.608 > read
0.422 > context 0.157 @ k=7. Target words never occur in the construction prompts (2/40 concepts
coincide with fit targets by genericity: airport, volleyball — implied, not named).

**Insights / next cards.**

- I1: steering for lens readouts lives in *processing-mode* directions that decouple a held
  concept from the surface text; content-entangled contrasts are actively harmful. Falsifiable:
  a third contrast with content decoupled (e.g. described concept + *different* carrier family)
  should again land in the 0.4–0.7 band.
- I2: the suppression arm is load-bearing (hold-vs-none ≤ 0.294 vs hold-vs-suppress 0.422–0.784):
  the direction is "active holding" relative to "active exclusion", not relative to baseline.
  Next: a "white-bear on the category" direction (suppress vs neutral) should be ~−d_ℓ and
  reproduce the reversed control.
- I3: the sharp dose peak (WBS k≈6, UCS k≈7.4, width ≈ ±1 in k) says the push must exceed natural
  along-direction variation without saturating the state — consistent with WBS §8; a norm-matched
  random direction at the same push stays near baseline (0.108–0.118), so the effect is
  direction-specific, not a norm effect.

(score of record). Captures and candidate directions under /tmp/steer/ (episode scratch, not
archived). Method name: **unspoken-concept steering (UCS)**.

# Study cards (`<id>.card.yaml`)

The dashboard's Studies page lays each study out from a short card next to its notes: `S4.md` + `S4.card.yaml`.
The notes stay the full record; the card is what a reader sees first. A study without a card still shows (its notes
and its battery), just without the structured header, formula, diagram and result charts. Update the card when the
study's verdict changes; keep every number traceable to the notes.

```yaml
id: S4                          # = the notes file's stem
title: Cluster and nearest-neighbour means          # <= 8 words, no id
owner: A (j-lens-mean-c0), pilot-1
# notes: S6.md                 # optional: the notes file, when not <id>.md (a study written up inside another's)
status: finalist                # finalist | negative | diagnostic | closed | open
question: >                     # 1-2 sentences; inline maths as $...$
  Does a regime-conditioned mean beat one family mean, and can a label-free cluster replace the family label?
verdict: >                      # 2-4 sentences: the answer, with its main cost or caveat
  ...
tiles:                          # 2-4 headline numbers, verbatim from the notes
  - {label: "val strict, Δ vs fam", value: "+0.049", sub: "+0.020 without UM / DM"}
formulas:                       # how g is built: 1-3 display equations (KaTeX), each with a one-line note
  - latex: 'g(h) = \frac{1}{k}\sum_{r \in N_k(h)} r'
    note: "N_k(h): the k nearest fit read cells of any family (cosine), own group excluded."
diagram:                        # one of the kinds below
  kind: pool
  select: knn
  caption: "..."
split: val                      # the split the result charts read (val if the study has val arms, else fit)
arms: ["knnx8@fit|cos", "kmx64@fit|cos"]                 # main arms, exact out/eval names on that split
controls: ["shuf.knnx8@fit|cos", "rand.knnx8@fit|cos"]   # their controls on that split ([] if none)
insights:                       # 2-6, most important first
  - {lead: "Clusters recover the family label without being told", text: "..."}
next: ["S4d: a cross-language kNN ..."]                  # open follow-ups ([] if none)
explainer:                      # optional: an "In depth" section after Method, one block per step (S14 has one)
  - heading: "What the lens reads: one direction per token"
    text: >                     # markdown, inline maths as $...$ (use `|` when the text holds a list)
      ...
    equations: [{latex: 's_t(h) = r_t^{\top} h', note: "..."}]   # optional display equations under the text
    after: >                    # optional text under the equations
      ...
    figure: {kind: template_build, caption: "..."}               # optional diagram (kinds below)
    panel: s14_norms            # optional live panel (dashboard/explainers.py PANELS), reads out/analysis JSON only
    wide: true                  # text, then the figure / panel full width (default: side by side)
```

Notation (formulas and inline maths): $h$ = $h_l$, the read cell's residual at layer $l$; $g(h)$ the centre, read
as $J_l(h - g(h))$; $\mathcal{R}$ the reference cells; $\bar h_S = \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{r\in S} r$; $N_k(h)$ the $k$
nearest reference cells; $\mu_{\text{fam}}$ the family mean; $P_k$ a projection onto $k$ directions. Write LaTeX
that KaTeX renders (no `\newcommand`, no `align`; use `\begin{aligned}` if needed).

Diagram kinds (dashboard/figures.py, `study_*`):

| kind | params | draws |
|---|---|---|
| `pool` | `select`: family, cluster, knn, token, position, language, other_language, neutral, all; `exclude` (optional): own_sentence, own_group | a cloud of reference cells, the subset g averages highlighted, its mean, and h - g |
| `subspace` | `k` | a family cloud with its top principal axes; g = family mean + h's component along them |
| `layer` | `lag`, `axis` (layer or position) | g taken from the cell's own state `lag` layers earlier (axis layer), or `lag` token positions earlier at the same layer (axis position) |
| `word` | `word` | the state of a category word (e.g. "language") subtracted from h |
| `probe` | `left`, `right` (short labels), `left_text`, `right_text` (the prompts) | two prompts side by side (a control: e.g. self-described vs quoted) |
| `maps` | – | the J-lens and J++ maps read from one state (map comparison) |
| `bridge` | – | a two-hop chain: prompt -> bridge -> answer, and which step a centre removes |

content.text:
Done. **Task `jlens-steer-assoc-017` complete: fit pass@10 0.1275 → 0.7843, threshold passed, all submission checks green.**

## What happened

**Calibration (the trap and the anchor).** The reading list contains `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md` — WBS, an existing method that solves exactly this task (think/don't-think stance contrast over a *named* concept, layers 20–24, large dose). Since the task forbids reproducing existing methods, I reproduced it as a control anchor: 53 DM dev-bank pairs + the paper's absolute per-layer steps → **0.686** at `prefix` k=6 (0.43 read / 0.14 context — matching the paper's position ablation, which also revealed what the server's position names mean).

**Finding the new method.** I tested ~15 self-authored contrasts. Everything that entangles the concept with the surface text is null-to-harmful: naming continuations (0.05–0.07), tip-and-pencil and question stances on the passage (0.05–0.07), hold/don't-track on the evocative passages themselves (≤0.12), even the white-bear suppression variant (0.04). The decoupled carrier structure works — a named concept on my own content scores 0.451 — and the concept word can be removed entirely:

> **Unspoken-concept steering (UCS).** 20 pairs I authored, each a *description* ("the sport played with a shuttlecock") + a neutral carrier sentence. **Hold**: "Keep in mind {description} as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: '{carrier}'" vs **Suppress**: "Do not try to think of any {category} as you write…" The concept is never named in either condition. d_ℓ = carrier-cell mean difference (ℓ = 20–24), added at all prompt positions with k = 7.4 → **fit 0.7843** (80/102; log10 rank 2.33 → 0.73).

Controls at the same dose: reversed sign **0.0098**, random direction **0.1176**, hold-without-suppress ≤ 0.294 (the suppression arm is load-bearing). The dose curve peaks sharply at k = 7.4, WBS-like. Target words never appear in the construction prompts (2 of my 40 concepts coincide with fit targets by pure genericity — implied, not named).

**Deliverables** (committed locally on `iteration`, not pushed):
- `submission/vectors.pt` (layers 20–24), `submission/contribution.md` (293 words, cites Turner/Panickssery/Todd/Raman), `submission/submission.json` — scored via `eval/submit.py`, re-verified with `eval/test_submission.py` (4/4, re-run reproduces 0.7843)
- `notes/iteration-anthony/studies/S25.md` + `S25.card.yaml` + a `mu-log.md` entry, recording the full candidate table and the mechanism insights (mode must decouple concept from surface text; the suppression condition is what makes the direction; direction-specificity confirmed by the norm-matched random control)
